desc: Parse the input: read T test cases, each with N and sequence A.

Initial DP attempt dp[i] = min(dp[i-1]+1, merge with previous same-value occurrence) — passes samples 1,2 but WRONG on sample 3 (gives 6, expected 8): it lets interspersed non-v elements vanish for free.
Second attempt charging 2 ops per interspersed non-v element — WRONG on sample 1 (gives 5, expected 3): interspersed elements can share deletion ops among themselves (recursive subproblem).
Establish the exact model: cost = (#deletion ops) + (#swaps) = (#chunks) + (#inversions over deletion-time assignment); each value's occurrences split into consecutive chunks with increasing times.
Build a brute-force solver (BFS over sequence states for N≤7) to produce ground-truth answers.
Derive candidate DP dp[i] = (i - cnt_v(i)) + min_j(dp[j] - j + cnt_v(j)) with per-value running minimum; validated vs BFS for all arrays N≤7 over alphabet {1,2,3} and all three samples (3, 4, 8).

Independently re-verify: (a) proved the WLOG that the last deletion op contains A[i-1] and that interspersed non-v elements cost exactly 1 op + 1 swap each; (b) extended BFS validation to N≤8 full ternary alphabet, N≤12 binary alphabet, distinct-value cases, and 3000 random arrays up to N=14 — DP matched BFS optimum in every case.
Finalize the O(sum N) stdin/stdout implementation (current solution code) and confirm sample outputs 3, 4, 8.
